title: Electric Furnace
model_title: Electric Arc Furnace (AC, Three Graphite Electrodes)

introduction.definition: An electric arc furnace (EAF) melts steel scrap or direct-reduced iron with electric arcs. A transformer supplies very high current to three graphite electrodes; arcs form between the electrode tips and the charge. Electrode height is regulated to hold the arc. The melt is refined and tapped through a bottom tap hole.
key_points: Foamy slag shields walls and improves efficiency
introduction.summary: An electric arc furnace melts steel scrap or direct-reduced iron using electric arcs between three graphite electrodes and the charge. A transformer supplies very high currents; the electrode height is regulated hydraulically to hold the arc. The melt is refined and then tapped.

temperature.description: The arcs between the electrode tips and the scrap/bath are extremely hot (thousands of °C) and melt the charge; liquid steel is typically tapped at around 1600–1650 °C. Water-cooled panels and roof protect the shell; foamy slag shields the panels from arc radiation.

video_tutorials.title: Electric Furnace — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Electric Furnace.
An electric arc furnace (EAF) melts steel scrap or direct-reduced iron with electric arcs.
A transformer supplies very high current to three graphite electrodes; arcs form between the electrode tips and the charge.
Electrode height is regulated to hold the arc.
Typical applications include steel making from scrap (mini-mills); stainless and special steels; foundries.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Shell, Refractory Hearth & Water-Cooled Wall Panels, Water-Cooled Roof with Refractory Delta & Electrode Ports (swings aside for charging).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Electric Furnace works.
Scrap is charged with the roof swung aside.
The transformer supplies high current to the electrodes.
Arcs between electrodes and scrap melt the charge.
Electrode regulation keeps the arc length steady.
The molten steel is tapped through the bottom tap.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The arcs between the electrode tips and the scrap/bath are extremely hot (thousands of °C) and melt the charge; liquid steel is typically tapped at around 1600–1650 °C.

video_tutorials.title: Electric Furnace — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Electric Furnace.
Inspect panels for leaks, electrode joints.
Refractory gunning/repair.
Replace roof/panels; transformer maintenance.
Watch for water leak into furnace: steam, explosion risk. Common cause: panel cracks.
Watch for electrode breakage: arc loss. Common cause: scrap cave-in, joint failure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
